title: しか: the inverted selection
summary: しか picks a noun and then makes everything else the subject, which is why the verb must be negative.

blocks.text: **しか** looks like a simple "only", but its structure is unusual. Think of the invert button in a photo editor: you select an object, press invert, and now everything except it is selected. That is what しか does with the **main carriage**.
私しかいない。 Nobody other than me is here.

The main carriage is not 私 but "everyone except me", and the engine says that group is **not** here. That is why しか always needs a negative engine. Like か, しか pushes out が (we never say がしか). It also selects for relevance: it means "no other people", not "no trees or birds either". For the difference from だけ, see lesson 33.
しか replaces が and を, but every other particle stays, and しか goes right after it.

blocks.jp: このパンは駅の店でしか買えない。
blocks.en: You can only buy this bread at the shop in the station.

blocks.text: A counter works as an adverb. When しか marks it, it flips the amount, not the subject.

blocks.jp: コップが一つしかない。

blocks.text: コップが一つしかない。 The subject stays; the counter is flipped.
The subject (コップ) stays; しか takes "one" and inverts it to "every amount but one", and those do not exist.
In speech しか can follow a whole action: "every other course of action does not exist", i.e. "there is nothing for it but to ...".

blocks.en: I have no choice but to go to bed.

blocks.text: This famous line plays with しか and the receptive (lesson 13) of 叱る, "to scold". The pun is that 鹿 (deer) and しか sound alike.

blocks.jp: 奈良なら鹿しか叱られない。
blocks.en: In Nara, only the deer don't get scolded. (a pun on 鹿 and しか)

items: **しか** selects a noun, then flips it: everything else is the main carriage.
しか replaces が and を, but keeps other particles (駅でしか).

questions.instruction: What must the engine of a しか sentence be?
questions.note: しか flips the main carriage, so the engine says that group is not here.
しか needs a negative engine: ない.
questions.en: I have only 1000 yen in my bag.

questions.prompt: 箱にりんごが二つ＿＿ない。
questions.note: A counter marked by しか flips the amount.
questions.en: There are only two apples in the box.

questions.instruction: What does the main carriage stand for?
questions.note: しか inverts: everyone except him is not here.
Like か, しか pushes out が.
Everyone except Yamada does not exist.

questions.instruction: Which sentence means "I have only one pen"?
questions.note: A counter + しか + a negative engine.

questions.instruction: Which two particles does しか usually take the place of?
questions.note: しか replaces が and を but keeps other particles.

questions.instruction: Which one means "I can buy it only at the station"?
questions.note: で is kept, and しか goes after it with a negative engine.

questions.prompt: りんごが三つしかない。
questions.note: しか takes "three" and inverts it to every other amount, which do not exist.
Verb + しかない: nothing for it but to.
questions.en: There is nothing for it but to go home.

options: I have no choice but to do it
questions.note: Every other course of action does not exist.
questions.en: There is nothing to do but do it.

questions.instruction: Does the sentence say the desks and chairs are absent?
questions.prompt: 教室には先生しかいなかった。
options: No: it means no other people
questions.note: しか selects for relevance: other people, not furniture.
questions.en: There was only the teacher in the classroom.

questions.instruction: Tap the noun that しか selects
questions.note: 野菜 is taken, and everything else is flipped.

questions.instruction: Tap the counter that しか flips
questions.note: 三時間 is flipped: every other amount did not happen.
questions.en: Yesterday I slept only three hours.

questions.note: しか always needs a negative engine.
A counter + しか + a negative engine.

questions.prompt: There is only one bank near the station.
questions.note: The counter 一つ is marked by しか.
questions.en: There is only one bank near the station.

questions.prompt: I have no choice but to wait here.
questions.note: Verb + しかない.
questions.en: I have no choice but to wait here.

options: 先生がしか来なかった
先生しかが来なかった
questions.note: しか pushes out が and needs a negative engine.

questions.prompt: ここは日本語しか話せない。
options: Only Japanese can be spoken here
questions.note: しか keeps the selected noun and negates the rest.
questions.en: You can speak only Japanese here.

questions.instruction: How does しか differ from だけ?
options: しか needs a negative engine; だけ does not
だけ needs a negative engine; しか does not
しか is only for people
questions.note: しか flips the selection, so its engine is negative.
